meta.title: Mumbai birth certificate (copy of a registered birth) grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the corporation's own quick link 'Application for Birth Certificate' returned HTTP 403 'Service cannot be reached' on the access date on both portal.mcgm.gov.in and www.mcgm.gov.in, so the online application route could not be reached at all; the Public Health Department FAQ that carries every fee figure has no visible date on its face and its file metadata gives a creation date of 10 September 2018, so it is treated as potentially outdated official material; the Birth/Death page that links it displays 'Last updated on 31/12/2016'; the downloadable application form is a scanned image with no text layer, so any document list printed on it could not be read; the citizen portal application surface itself requires login and was not entered. Do not submit personal data through this ledger. Audit limitation carried unresolved: no archive snapshot was captured at access time for the observed HTTP 403 on the birth-certificate quick link or for the ward-list portal runtime error, so neither observation is preserved in any archive; the existing Wayback copies of those routes predate the access date and show different content.

agencies.name: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Public Health Department

scenarios.label: Mumbai birth certificate copy
scenarios.summary: A parent resident in Mumbai seeks a certified copy or first certificate of a birth already registered in the city's civil register, by the municipal civil-registration route, public entry, online where offered and counter route otherwise. Delayed registration, name inclusion, corrections, births outside the city and hospital-side registration steps are excluded.

sources.title: FAQ on Birth and Death - Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Public Health Department
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: the document's own masthead reads 'MUNICIPAL CORPORATION OF GREATER MUMBAI, PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT' and it is signed 'sd/- Executive Health Officer'. It carries no visible date on its face; the PDF metadata records a creation date of 2018-09-10, which is recorded as the best available dating and as a limitation, so claims from it are graded C as potentially outdated official material. Six pages in English, Marathi and Hindi; only the English section is quoted. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20240616125010/https://portal.mcgm.gov.in/irj/go/km/docs/documents/MCGM%20Department%20List/Public%20Health%20Department/Docs/FAQ%20Birth%20and%20Death%20Registration%20-%20English,%20Marathi,%20Hindi.pdf (2024-06-16); no new capture was pushed from this run. Limitation: that snapshot predates the access date, so it does not preserve the source as reviewed on 2026-09-06.

sources.title: Application for Birth Certificate quick link - portal error response
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: the page renders inside the 'MyBMC' shell of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation. Visible date: none is shown; the error page carries no publication or revision date. Direct current observation of a public official interface: the route returns 'Service cannot be reached', 'URL call was terminated because the corresponding service is not available', 'HTTP 403 - Forbidden'. The same result was observed on the parallel host www.mcgm.gov.in. Limitation: an error page is undated by nature, so this records the route's state on the access date only. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20251228084813/https://portal.mcgm.gov.in/irj/portal/anonymous/qlbirthcertificate?guest_user=english (2025-12-28); no new capture was pushed from this run. Limitation: that snapshot predates the access date and does not preserve the failure observed on 2026-09-06.

claims.text: The MCGM Public Health Department FAQ states that for birth events occurring after 1 January 2016 a charge of Rs. 6 applies for each copy.
claims.notes: An amount a citizen pays, for the period that covers a birth registered in recent years. Graded C because the document is undated on its face and its file metadata dates it to 2018. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the reason the FAQ gives for the charge is asserted separately.

claims.text: The same FAQ attributes that charge to certificates being generated from the Central Government's Civil Registration System software on crs.orgi.gov.in.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_fee_post_2016_six_rupees. The reason given for the charge is separately checkable from the amount.

claims.text: The MCGM Public Health Department FAQ states that for birth events occurring before 31 December 2015 the first copy of the birth certificate is free of charge to relatives after producing necessary documents.
claims.notes: An explicit zero, recorded as a stated value under protocol section 3.

claims.text: The MCGM Public Health Department FAQ states that for birth events occurring before 31 December 2015 a person other than a relative pays Rs. 20 plus Rs. 2 searching charges, and Rs. 30 for each further copy.
claims.notes: The scoped applicant is a parent, so the relative rate applies; the non-relative rate is recorded because it is part of the same published schedule.

claims.text: The MCGM Public Health Department FAQ states that citizens can obtain a birth certificate from the Civic Facility Center of the ward office after applying in the prescribed format.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the collection point, the payment step and the counter hours.

claims.text: The same FAQ states that the necessary charges are paid at that Civic Facility Center.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_obtain_at_ward_cfc. The payment step is separately checkable from the collection point.

claims.text: The same FAQ gives the Civic Facility Center hours as working days between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_obtain_at_ward_cfc. Counter opening hours, not a processing duration.

claims.text: The MCGM Public Health Department FAQ states that a birth occurring in a hospital or at home is registered in the ward office of the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai in whose area the event occurred.
claims.notes: A jurisdiction rule that identifies which office holds the record.

claims.text: The MCGM Public Health Department FAQ states that a birth certificate is issued by the Registrar of the local government institution of the place where the event occurred.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the consequence for an event outside Mumbai is asserted separately.

claims.text: The same FAQ states that a certificate cannot be obtained in Mumbai for an event that happened outside Mumbai.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_issued_by_registrar_of_place. The territorial consequence is separately checkable from the issuing rule.

claims.text: The MCGM Public Health Department FAQ on birth and death is issued over the signature block of the Executive Health Officer.
claims.notes: A designation, recorded as the officer under whose authority the guidance is published rather than as the officer who decides an individual application.

claims.text: BMC's Birth/Death citizen page states that the Health Department is the administrative department of BMC responsible for birth and death registrations and the issue of birth and death certificates.
claims.notes: Graded C because the page displays a last-updated date of 31 December 2016.

claims.text: BMC's Birth/Death citizen page offers the birth certificate application form as a download under the heading 'Online Applications - Apply', linking to a PDF file.
claims.notes: The linked file was retrieved and is a scanned image with no text layer, so nothing printed on the form could be read in this environment; that is a limitation on this run's reach, not a claim about the form's content.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ states that the applicant may visit the nearest Citizen Facilitation Center established by the Municipal Corporation belonging to any of the 24 wards of BMC.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the counter route, the online route and the proviso common to both.

claims.text: The same FAQ states that the applicant may instead fill in the online application form on the Citizen Portal.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_apply_at_cfc_or_online. The online route is separately checkable from the counter route.

claims.text: The same FAQ makes both routes available provided the applicant's birth is already registered with BMC.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_apply_at_cfc_or_online. The proviso 'provided applicant's birth is already registered with BMC' matches this scenario's trigger and is the part of the sentence the eligibility cell rests on.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ states that birth records after the year 1996 are available in the system.
claims.notes: A rule that decides which route applies: online for post-1996 records, the ward counter otherwise. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the post-1996 rule, the pre-1996 qualification and the direction to the ward.

claims.text: The same FAQ states that records prior to 1996 may not be available in the system as of now.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_records_after_1996_online. The pre-1996 qualification is separately checkable from the post-1996 rule.

claims.text: The same FAQ directs an applicant whose record is not in the system to the nearest ward for further help.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_records_after_1996_online. The fallback route is separately checkable from the availability rule.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ states that the applicant searches the registration record by entering the registration number provided by the hospital, nursing home or maternity home.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the alternative search fields are asserted separately by claim_mumbai_birth_search_by_registration_number_2.

claims.text: Where the registration number is not known the same FAQ allows the search to use gender, date of birth, ward, father's name, mother's name or hospital name.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_search_by_registration_number. This fragment carries the FAQ's published list of alternative search fields, which is one published list and is waived on the manifest entry.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ answers the question whether a fee must be paid without stating any amount.
claims.notes: A payment step without an amount; recorded to show where the citizen is left, not to support the cost cell, which rests on the Public Health Department schedule. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; what the answer does describe is asserted separately.

claims.text: That answer describes only how to pay, saying that online payment can be made by net banking from the listed banks through the payment gateway.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_fee_topic_without_amount. What the FAQ does say is separately checkable from what it omits.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ states that an applicant at the Citizen Facilitation Center needs to submit the duly signed application form along with required documents, without naming any document.
claims.notes: The topic of documents is named without telling the citizen what is required.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ states that the Citizen Facilitation Center agent collects the necessary fees and required documents.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; what the applicant receives at the end is asserted separately by claim_mumbai_birth_cfc_issues_certificate_and_receipt_2, which is the fragment the after-submission cell rests on.

claims.text: The same FAQ states that as a final step the agent prints and issues the certificate and a fee receipt to the applicant.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_cfc_issues_certificate_and_receipt. A result and a receipt the applicant receives after submitting at the counter.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ states that the applicant chooses a mode of delivery, either collecting the certificate from the ward or having it couriered to the applicant's address.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the courier period is asserted separately by claim_mumbai_birth_delivery_mode_choice_2.

claims.text: The same FAQ states that a couriered certificate will arrive within the days stipulated by the Department of Posts.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_delivery_mode_choice. The delivery period is expressed by reference to another department's unstated schedule, so it carries no figure the citizen can act on.

claims.text: The corporation's own quick link 'Application for Birth Certificate' returned an error page reading 'Service cannot be reached' on the access date.
claims.notes: Direct current observation of a public official interface. Recorded as observed rather than replaced by a homepage. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the three separately checkable parts of the observation.

claims.text: The same error page read 'URL call was terminated because the corresponding service is not available' and 'HTTP 403 - Forbidden'.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_quicklink_http_403. The error text and status code are separately checkable from the page's headline message.

claims.text: The same result was observed on both portal.mcgm.gov.in and www.mcgm.gov.in.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_quicklink_http_403. That both hosts fail is separately checkable from what the failure says.

claims.text: BMC publishes a ward list naming its twenty-four wards.
claims.notes: The list names wards; it does not give a Civic Facility Center address or a contact for the birth-certificate route.

claims.text: Whether the Rs. 6 per copy figure still applies on the access date is not established by any reviewed public page: the only route that states it is undated on its face, and no current BMC page restates any amount.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.

claims.text: BMC's birth-certificate application FAQ directs the applicant to the Citizen Portal to fill in the online form, and the citizen portal application surface was not entered in this run.
claims.notes: Boundary statement, recorded as a limitation and not used to support any positive cell value. The observation is the FAQ's instruction; the boundary was not crossed, and in any case the corporation's own entry point to that surface returned HTTP 403 on the access date.

claims.text: BMC's ward list page rendered a portal runtime error reading 'An exception occurred while processing your request.' on the access date.
claims.notes: Split by audit from claim_mumbai_birth_ward_list_published for atomicity under protocol section 1. Direct current observation of a public official interface, graded B under the section 4 table and the public-workflow rule in section 1. Split again during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the error, its instruction and its exception ID.

claims.text: The same error page instructed the reader to send the exception ID to the portal administrator.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_ward_list_runtime_error. The instruction is separately checkable from the error message.

claims.text: The exception ID displayed on the access date was 10:21_06/09/26_302592051.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_mumbai_birth_ward_list_runtime_error. A system-generated diagnostic identifier printed on a public error page. The page was read without a login and no personal data was entered.
